description.summary: private privileged window management interface

protocol.description: This protocol allows privileged clients to manage window layering, relative stacking orders within layers, exclusive edge reservations for shell components (taskbars), and activation without tokens.

interface.name: wex_window_manager_v1

description.summary: manager interface for privileged window controls

interface.description: Allows obtaining a wex_window_v1 interface for an xdg_toplevel. Only advertised to privileged clients on the wex-shell socket.

description.summary: destroy the manager object
create a wex_window_v1 from an xdg_toplevel

request.name: get_foreign

description.summary: observe supplemental native window metadata

request.description: The toplevel must belong to this connection's standard zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1 inventory. Metadata and ordinary controls remain on that standard interface. An ineligible or closed toplevel yields a closed object without a token. This request neither adopts the view nor changes its decoration or focus.

event.name: native_environment

description.summary: compositor-owned native application endpoints

event.description: Sent once on binding. Native programs use the normal Wayland socket, rather than inherit the shell's privileged socket. xwayland_display is empty if XWayland is unavailable; remove DISPLAY in that case. These values belong to this compositor, not an enclosing nested session. Launch and D-Bus activation environments must agree on these endpoints.

request.name: get_render_surface

description.summary: privileged cross-connection Wine rendering surface

request.description: Assigns a role to a producer-owned surface. Only the private endpoint may create it. The parent is selected by an existing unpredictable frame handle, not a raw HWND or caller-supplied process identifier.

description.summary: material drawn behind a window's translucent parts

entry.name: blur
entry.summary: blurred view of what is behind (Aero glass)

entry.name: acrylic
entry.summary: stronger blur with a tint

entry.name: mica
entry.summary: blurred desktop wallpaper with a tint

entry.name: gradient
entry.summary: the tint alone, no blur

entry.name: shadow
entry.summary: soft shadow outside the window

entry.name: dark
entry.summary: dark default tint

entry.name: tint
entry.summary: the tint argument replaces the default tint

entry.name: region
entry.summary: the backdrop covers the given region only

request.name: set_effects

description.summary: set the DWM effects of a window by shared handle

request.description:
Privileged clients only (the private endpoint). The window is named by the shared handle from wex_window_v1.handle, so the Wine shell can set the effects of any Wine window, not only its own. An unknown or stale handle is a harmless no-op. The request replaces all effects of the window: all-zero arguments clear them.
corner_radius is clamped to 0..32 like wex_window_v1.set_corner_radius (which stays, for a window's owner). tint is straight (non-premultiplied) 0xAARRGGBB, used when the tint flag is set. region is in window logical coordinates (left, top, right, bottom) and used when the region flag is set. The backdrop is drawn behind the window's own pixels, so it shows through only where the window is translucent. Without compositor support for a material (blur, acrylic, mica) the compositor draws the tint alone.

entry.name: has_source
entry.summary: the source rectangle is used, else the whole source window

request.name: set_thumbnails

description.summary: replace the list of live window thumbnails

request.description:
Privileged clients only. The compositor draws a scaled live copy of each source window inside its destination window, above the destination's own content (DwmRegisterThumbnail on Windows). The list replaces the previous one; an empty array removes all thumbnails.
The array holds records of 104 bytes in native byte order: char dest[32] shared handle of the destination window (no NUL) char src[32] shared handle of the source window (no NUL) uint32 flags thumbnail_flags uint32 opacity 0..255 int32 dest_rect[4] left, top, right, bottom in the destination's logical window coordinates int32 source_rect[4] left, top, right, bottom in the source's logical window coordinates (with has_source) Records with an unknown or stale handle, a source equal to its destination, or an empty rectangle are skipped, so the list may refer to windows that are gone. A minimized or hidden source keeps showing its last contents. At most 80 records are used.

request.name: set_peek

description.summary: hide every window except a target and the windows kept

request.description: Privileged clients only (Aero Peek). While a target is set, every window that is neither the target nor in keep (an array of 32 byte shared handles) is not drawn; the target is drawn even when minimized. An empty target handle ends the peek. Stale handles are ignored. The compositor ends the peek when the client disconnects.

event.name: frame

description.summary: a frame was presented

event.description: Sent to the manager (privileged clients) for each frame of the primary output, with a counter that increases by one per frame and a CLOCK_MONOTONIC time: the display time of the frame when the output backend reports presentation (the wlr_output present event), else the time of the commit. The shell uses it as the frame clock of DwmFlush.

arg.name: frame
arg.summary: low 32 bits of the frame counter

enum.name: shell_key_modifiers

description.summary: modifiers of a shell key combination

enum.description: The values of the X11 and wlroots modifier masks.

request.name: set_shell_keys

description.summary: the key combinations that belong to the shell

request.description:
Privileged clients only. Replaces the list of key combinations the shell takes from native programs (the Windows key, Ctrl+Esc, Alt+Tab, Alt+F4), as an X11 window manager takes them with passive key grabs.
While a client that is not connected to the private endpoint has the keyboard and the session is not locked, a press that matches a listed combination goes to this manager as a shell_key event instead of to the client, and so does every key after it until that key is released (with hold_keyboard, until release_keyboard). Clients on the private endpoint, the Wine programs, keep their keys. Modifier state still reaches the focused client through wl_keyboard.modifiers.
The array holds records of 8 bytes in native byte order: uint32 keysym the key's keysym without modifiers (level 1) uint32 modifiers shell_key_modifiers that must be held exactly (Caps Lock and Num Lock do not count), or 0xffffffff for the key with any modifiers At most 32 records are used. An empty array removes the list; it also ends with this manager object.

request.name: hold_keyboard

description.summary: keep sending every key to the shell

request.description: While keys go to the shell (after a shell_key press), they go on doing so until release_keyboard, also once the key that started it is released. The shell's Alt+Tab holds the keyboard until Alt is released.

request.name: release_keyboard

description.summary: stop holding the keyboard

request.description: Ends hold_keyboard. Keys go to the focused client again once the key that started the sending is no longer down.

event.name: shell_key

description.summary: a key taken from a native program

event.description: keysym is the key's keysym without modifiers (level 1), modifiers the shell_key_modifiers held when the key changed state, and state a wl_keyboard.key_state (1 pressed, 0 released).

request.name: set_parent

description.summary: attach or detach within a privileged frame

request.description: Coordinates are frame-content logical units. Width and height bound the rendering region. Empty, unknown or stale handles detach without changing frame input/focus. Frame destruction revokes the attachment. The surface inherits the frame's position, visibility and minimization.

interface.name: wex_window_v1

description.summary: window controls interface

interface.description: Provides operations for stacking, layering, shell edge reservation, and direct activation.

entry.name: normal
entry.summary: normal application window

entry.name: topmost
entry.summary: above normal windows

entry.name: desktop
entry.summary: below everything, not in window cycling

entry.name: shell
entry.summary: above topmost, not in window cycling

entry.name: none
entry.summary: no exclusive edge

entry.name: top
entry.summary: top edge

entry.name: bottom
entry.summary: bottom edge

entry.name: left
entry.summary: left edge

entry.name: right
entry.summary: right edge

description.summary: destroy this window object
place above sibling in the same layer
place below sibling in the same layer
lower to the bottom of its layer
assign window to a layer
reserve edge for shell window
give keyboard focus and raise within its layer

event.name: handle

description.summary: shared opaque window handle

event.description: Sent once when the object is created. This compositor-generated token identifies the window until its view or control object is destroyed. Privileged clients may share it across connections. Treat it as opaque.

request.name: place_above_handle

description.summary: place above a shared sibling handle

request.description: Like place_above, but accepts a sibling from another privileged client. Unknown, stale, self, or different-layer handles are harmless no-ops.

request.name: place_below_handle

description.summary: place below a shared sibling handle

request.description: Like place_below, but accepts a sibling from another privileged client. Unknown, stale, self, or different-layer handles are harmless no-ops.

request.name: restore

description.summary: restore without changing keyboard focus

request.description: Clear minimization without activating or raising the window. Use activate instead when the client also wants to give keyboard focus.

entry.name: prepared
entry.summary: reserved; native composition and focus unchanged

request.name: associate_foreign

description.summary: reserve a native view and live controller for this frame

request.description: Both opaque handles must identify the same eligible native view and a live privileged observer. Only one frame may reserve a native view. An empty pair releases this frame's reservation. Unknown, stale, mismatched or busy handles return unavailable without replacing an existing reservation. Repeating the current pair is idempotent. A prepared association does not change native decoration, scene nodes, geometry or focus. Rendering/input preparation must precede adoption. Controller, native-view or frame destruction releases the reservation.

request.name: commit_foreign

description.summary: compose a prepared native/frame pair

request.description: The rectangle is the native client area in frame root-surface logical coordinates. Both views must be mapped with matching native client dimensions. The frame root renders only outside this rectangle; native buffers and popup trees remain in the compositor scene. CSD/borderless natives require a full-surface cutout. Invalid or not-ready requests leave the reservation unchanged and return not_ready. Reservation destruction detaches the group, restores native decorations and hides the obsolete proxy frame. This request does not activate either view.

entry.name: none
entry.summary: query only, or focus outside this group

entry.name: native
entry.summary: activate native content

entry.name: frame
entry.summary: temporary frame keyboard focus

entry.name: restore_native
entry.summary: guarded native focus restoration, request only

request.name: set_foreign_focus

description.summary: request physical focus with a client activation epoch

request.description: Requests apply only to an active group. Native activates and raises the group. Frame and restore_native apply only while physical focus already belongs to this group, so a late frame-menu completion cannot steal focus from another application. None queries without changing focus. Every request replies with foreign_focus reporting actual focus and echoing epoch, even if the requested transition was rejected. Unknown targets leave focus unchanged. The client must also check its current logical foreground window before restoring native focus. Minimized groups reject focus requests. Restore them explicitly using activate or restore; a delayed focus request must not undo a minimize.

event.name: foreign_focus

description.summary: observed physical keyboard focus for this group

event.description: Sent after requests and on seat keyboard focus changes, including native popups and frame subsurfaces. Epoch is the most recent request's epoch, or zero before the first request. Target is none, native or frame; restore_native is never reported. Detached groups report none. This event acknowledges physical focus, not a Win32 foreground transition.

request.name: uncommit_foreign

description.summary: detach content while retaining its reservation

request.description: Detaches an active group, restores native decorations and hides the obsolete frame. Replies with detached even if no group was active. The prepared reservation remains available for a later commit after matching buffers and client geometry are ready. Does not activate.

request.name: configure_foreign

description.summary: numbered commit for asynchronous controllers

request.description: Same geometry and validation as commit_foreign. Replies with configured_foreign after reporting observed group state, distinguishing request completion from unsolicited detached notifications. Serial is opaque to the server. An active group may change its client rectangle without detaching. The server retains the previous roots until the updated frame and matching native content have both committed, then replies ACTIVE.

request.name: capture_foreign_pointer

description.summary: temporary pointer capture for a hosted frame loop

request.description: Capture requires an active group, physical frame keyboard focus and the current focus epoch. Pointer events then target the frame surface, including outside its input region. Release never changes keyboard focus. Capture is revoked on focus loss, group detach or resource destruction. Stale requests cannot acquire capture or displace another frame.

event.name: foreign_pointer_capture

description.summary: capture acknowledgement or asynchronous revocation

event.description: Acknowledges every request. Revocation uses the epoch that acquired capture. Captured is zero or one; keyboard focus is reported separately.

entry.name: accepted
entry.summary: constrained request, not a buffer completion

entry.name: acknowledged
entry.summary: native xdg configure acknowledged, buffer not yet committed

entry.name: native_ready
entry.summary: actual native client geometry, awaiting matching frame

entry.name: complete
entry.summary: matching frame and native buffers made visible atomically

entry.name: rolling_back
entry.summary: restore this old geometry and submit its matching frame

entry.name: cancelled
entry.summary: old matching buffers and geometry restored

entry.name: superseded
entry.summary: a newer request replaced this transaction

entry.name: unavailable
entry.summary: unsupported client, invalid geometry or missing frame capture

entry.name: stale
entry.summary: serial is no longer current

entry.name: failed
entry.summary: bounded rollback failed; normal native scene restored

request.name: resize_foreign

description.summary: negotiate a hosted native size without exposing mismatched buffers

request.description: Requires an active group and pointer capture for the physically focused frame at its current focus epoch. Initially supported for xdg toplevels; other native types reply unavailable. Serial is nonzero and increases modulo 2^32 within this frame resource. Coordinates are the desired native client rectangle in compositor logical layout units, not Wine pixels. Edges use wlroots edge bits: top=1, bottom=2, left=4, right=8; opposing edges are invalid. Left/top retain the desired right/bottom anchor after constraints or client-selected sizes. Current native hints are read at request time. Accepted, acknowledged and native_ready are distinct. Old matching root buffers remain visible until commit_foreign_resize. Popup and subsurface ownership remains unchanged. A newer request supersedes the old one while retaining the original rollback geometry. No request here changes focus or implicitly activates a window.

request.name: commit_foreign_resize

description.summary: publish an already committed matching frame

request.description: Send after receiving native_ready and committing the corresponding Wine frame buffer, in that connection's request order. The rectangle is the native client hole in frame surface logical units. All four saved frame margins and the actual native size must match. Early, stale or mismatched requests reply unavailable/stale without changing the scene; they may be retried. Complete is sent only after the atomic handover. During rollback the same request submits the restored frame and produces cancelled. Controllers must not coalesce these completion events.

request.name: cancel_foreign_resize

description.summary: restore the original group before releasing capture

request.description: Current serial only. Rolling_back supplies the old geometry; native configure acknowledgement and native_ready follow as usual. Submit the restored frame with commit_foreign_resize before releasing capture or returning native focus. Loss of physical frame focus also starts rollback. A two-second timeout starts rollback; a second timeout restores the ordinary native scene and reports failed. Detachment also reports failed.

event.name: foreign_resize

description.summary: serial-specific resize transition

event.description: Geometry is constrained for accepted/rolling_back, actual committed client geometry for native_ready/complete/cancelled, zero when unavailable or stale. Configure_serial is the separate native xdg configure serial, never the controller serial. Acknowledgement does not imply a buffer commit. Old requests cannot complete or cancel a newer transaction.

request.name: set_corner_radius

description.summary: set per-surface corner radius for window clipping

request.description: Sets the corner radius in pixels used to clip the window's corners when compositing. A radius of 0 disables clipping (sharp corners). The compositor clamps the radius to the range 0..32. Only the client that owns the surface may set its corner radius; requests from unprivileged clients or non-owners are rejected.

interface.name: wex_foreign_window_v1

description.summary: supplemental native window observation

interface.description: A compositor-generated token identifies a native view for its lifetime, across privileged connections. Tokens are never reused for another view. All geometry and size hints use compositor logical coordinates for the native client area. Each initial or changed snapshot ends with done. closed is terminal; requests other than destroy are ignored afterward.

entry.name: none
entry.summary: borderless native view

entry.name: client
entry.summary: application draws its frame

entry.name: server
entry.summary: eligible for a Wine frame

description.summary: request a fresh supplemental snapshot

event.name: controller_handle

description.summary: opaque handle valid only while this observer lives

event.description: A privileged frame on another connection may pair this handle with the native view token in associate_foreign. Unlike the view token, this handle is unique to the controller and becomes invalid on disconnect.

event.name: maximum_size

description.summary: native maximum client dimensions

event.description: Compositor logical coordinates, with zero meaning no limit on that axis. This supplements size_hints and belongs to the same done-delimited snapshot. Minima equal to nonzero maxima describe a fixed-size axis. Only managers bound at version 9 create version 9 observers; older clients keep their original event set and infer no maximum.
